claims: The Artemis II launch is currently targeted for Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II launch has a two-hour launch window opening at 6:24 p.m. EDT (22:24 UTC).
The Artemis II launch is from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The official 49-hour 40-minute countdown for the Artemis II launch began on Monday, March 30, at 4:44 p.m. EDT.
Teams are monitoring an 80% chance of favorable weather for the Artemis II launch.
Artemis II launch time is 6:24 p.m. EDT (3:24 p.m. PDT / 22:24 UTC).
Backup launch opportunities for Artemis II are available from April 2 through April 6.
An additional backup launch opportunity for Artemis II is available on April 30.
Artemis II is a 10-day crewed mission around the Moon.
Artemis II tests the Orion spacecraft.
Artemis II tests the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
On April 1 at 7:45 a.m. EDT, live coverage of propellant loading (tanking) begins on NASA's YouTube channel.
On April 1 at 12:50 p.m. EDT, full broadcast coverage begins on NASA+.
The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew will be the first humans to travel to the vicinity of the Moon in over 50 years.
